title: Clo Summit Bengaluru 2026: Threads Of Transformation
description:
That’s a wrap on an incredible CLO Summit Bengaluru 2026! 🇮🇳 A heartfelt thank you to our partners who joined us at the Bengaluru International Center for two days of deep, future-forward discussions on the digital fashion ecosystem. 🫶 

🫡 A massive shoutout to our incredible speakers for sharing their invaluable expertise! The energy was electric as we explored the transformative power of AI and workflow automation. ⚡

As we approach the 2026 fashion landscape, digital depth has officially replaced production capacity as the ultimate competitive moat. Success today requires more than just tool adoption. It demands transitioning from a "System of Record" to a "System-of-Action" mindset. True market leaders are using management-led strategies to turn structured 3D data into the definitive fuel for AI, real-time decision-making, and sustainable, scalable growth. Thank you for driving the technology forward with us. Here's to building the future together! 🚀

markdown_content: ## Threads of Transformation: AI-Driven Fashion Workflow This section introduces the idea of creating clothes that can be “dressed here” and frames the discussion around building a business workflow and understanding how AI can support day-to-day fashion work. It also highlights the broader goal: not only making garments, but improving how people dress. The speaker explains that the concept began with an idea for clothes that enable a more interactive or localized workflow (“clothes that we can dress here”). They describe meeting new people, discussing business concepts, and exploring how to take the idea further—specifically by understanding workflow processes and how they could be implemented in practice. A key theme is the emergence of AI in fashion and how it can be utilized in day-to-day workflows. The speaker emphasizes that clothing creation is part of life, but the focus extends beyond the garments themselves to the way people dress—suggesting that fashion transformation includes both production and user experience considerations. ## Workflow Development with 3D and AI This section covers the team’s transition into a 3D workflow, including their use of “Flow3D” (referred to as “flow 3D” in the transcript) and how they evaluate it through ongoing updates. The team states they are now working on “Flow3D” (written in the transcript as “flow 3D”). They mention attempting “Flow submit,” which they describe as helping them understand the workflow of the clothes. They also report that Flow3D is going well, particularly as new updates are received. The speaker’s perspective is that the outcome exceeded expectations: they did not anticipate working “this well” with Flow3D. This implies that the workflow integration and usability of the system are key factors in their assessment. ## Fit Production Focus and Team Learning This section highlights the importance of fit production and references a presentation by Aarya, describing it as especially interesting and relevant to the speaker’s experiences across organizations. A major point of interest is fit production, which the transcript notes was presented by “Aarya.” The speaker describes this segment as very interesting and says they could relate it to their own experiences and to “like-minded” individuals in different organizations. The implication is that the fit production process discussed in the presentation connects to real-world industry practices and challenges, and that the speaker found it applicable to multiple organizational contexts. ## Acknowledgments and Event Support This section contains gratitude directed toward the organizing team and acknowledges hands-on effort from participants. The speaker thanks the Kloer team for organizing the event and expresses appreciation for the hands and effort contributed by others.
